markdown:
## Protocol: I have a small biopsy of non-pregnant human endometrium and want to establish a reusable three-dimensional epithelial culture. Describe tissue processing, gland recovery, seeding in an extracellular matrix, routine feeding and serial passaging, and how to freeze and recover the resulting organoids. Focus on establishing and maintaining the culture.

### Overview

This protocol details the establishment, maintenance, passaging, and cryopreservation of a reusable three-dimensional epithelial culture derived from non-pregnant human endometrium. The process involves enzymatic digestion to recover glandular elements, embedding in Matrigel for organoid formation, routine expansion using a defined growth medium, and standard freezing protocols for long-term storage.

### Materials/Reagents

RPMI 1640 medium; Penicillin/Streptomycin; Collagenase V (0.4 mg/ml); Dispase II (1.25 U/ml); Fetal Calf Serum (FCS) 10%; Advanced DMEM/F12; N2 Supplement; B27 Supplement minus Vitamin A; Primocin (100 µg/ml); N-Acetyl-L-cysteine (1.25 mM); L-glutamine (2 mM); Recombinant human EGF (50 ng/ml); Recombinant human Noggin (100 ng/ml); Recombinant human Rspondin-1 (500 ng/ml); Recombinant human FGF-10 (100 ng/ml); Recombinant human HGF (50 ng/ml); ALK-4, -5, -7 inhibitor A83-01 (500 nM); Nicotinamide (10 nM); Matrigel; Cell Recovery Solution (Corning); Recovery cell culture freezing medium (Life Technologies).

### Equipment

Petri dishes; Scalpels; Forceps; 60 mL lidded disposable containers; Heated shaker; Phase-contrast microscope; 100 µm cell sieves; Plastic Pasteur pipettes; Universal tubes; Microcentrifuge (capable of 500g and 600g); Corning 48-well tissue culture plates; 1 mL pipette tips; Low-binding Eppendorf tubes; Low-retention pipette tips; Cryovials; 'Mr. Frosty' or similar controlled-rate freezing vessel; Liquid nitrogen storage system.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterile technique throughout all tissue processing, seeding, and passaging steps. Use antibiotic-supplemented media (Penicillin/Streptomycin, Primocin) to prevent bacterial contamination. Handle biological tissues with appropriate personal protective equipment. Ensure proper disposal of biohazardous waste.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-Experiment

1. Prepare basic wash medium by supplementing RPMI 1640 with penicillin/streptomycin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare collagenase/dispase solution containing 0.4 mg/ml collagenase V and 1.25 U/ml dispase II in RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 10% FCS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare expansion medium consisting of Advanced DMEM/F12 supplemented with N2 supplement, B27 supplement minus vitamin A, Primocin (100 µg/ml), N-Acetyl-L-cysteine (1.25 mM), L-glutamine (2 mM), recombinant human EGF (50 ng/ml), recombinant human Noggin (100 ng/ml), recombinant human Rspondin-1 (500 ng/ml), recombinant human FGF-10 (100 ng/ml), recombinant human HGF (50 ng/ml), ALK-4, -5, -7 inhibitor A83-01 (500 nM), and nicotinamide (10 nM). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Initiation of Culture

### Initiation of culture

1. Upon receipt, transfer tissue samples into the basic wash medium plus penicillin/streptomycin at room temperature and process within one hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Examine tissues macroscopically and discard non-decidual tissue. Select only tissue pieces larger than 1 cm³ that can be confidently identified as decidua compacta or decidua spongiosa. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Wash the selected tissue in basic culture medium with gentle stirring for 20 minutes to remove contaminating blood. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Transfer tissue to a petri dish. Using forceps, move tissue pieces to a clean dish and mince them with scalpels into 0.5–1 mm³ pieces. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Transfer the minced tissue to a 60 mL lidded, disposable container with sufficient diameter to allow mixing by agitation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Add 10–30 mL of warmed collagenase/dispase solution. Seal the lid and place the container in a heated shaker at 37°C with gentle shaking to digest the tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. Sample the digest after 20 minutes and subsequently at 10-minute intervals to check for free glandular elements. Stromal cells disaggregate faster than glands, dispersing into the supernatant while leaving intact tubular gland structures visible under phase-contrast microscopy. When these are abundant, dilute the enzyme/tissue mix with RPMI-1640 medium to minimize further disaggregation, transferring to a larger container if necessary. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
8. Swirl the container firmly (without shaking) and let it stand for 2 minutes to allow undigested tissue fragments to sediment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
9. Pass the supernatant through one or more 100 µm cell sieves. Wash the sieves thoroughly with RPMI-1640 medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
10. Invert the sieves over a petri dish and backwash the glandular elements from the membrane by forceful pipetting using a plastic Pasteur pipette. Transfer the backwashed glands to a universal tube and pellet by centrifugation at 500g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
11. Re-suspend the glandular elements in 1–2 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 medium. Gently pipette up and down several times to partially dissociate cells. Transfer to 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and pellet by centrifugation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
12. Remove the supernatant and estimate the volume of the pellet. Flick the tube to loosen the pellet and place it on ice for 2–3 minutes. Add 20 volumes of ice-cold Matrigel relative to the pellet volume and pipette gently to mix. Immediately return the tube to ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
13. Plate 20–25 µL drops of the Matrigel/cell suspension into the center of wells in Corning 48-well tissue culture plates. Place the plate in the incubator for 15 minutes to allow the Matrigel to set. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
14. Overlay each drop with 250 µL of Expansion Medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
15. Examine cultures for the appearance of hollow spheroids, replacing the expansion medium every 2–3 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
> **Operational constraint:** When spheroids/organoids are abundant, passage them as described below. Note: If there is dense material in the wells after 2 weeks with no visible spheroids, they should still be passaged at this stage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->

## Passaging

### Passaging

1. Without removing the culture medium, use a 1 mL pipette tip to scrape backwards and forwards across the growth surface of each well to detach the Matrigel drop into the medium. Transfer the contents of four wells into a single 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 minutes to pellet. Remove the supernatant and add approximately 150 µL of Advanced DMEM/F12 to each tube. Pipette up and down 300 times through a small bore pipette tip to break up the organoids and Matrigel without using excessive force. An electronic pipetter with a ‘mix' function and uptake volume set to 150 µL is recommended. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. Add 1 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 minutes. Remove the supernatant. Add 150 µL of Advanced DMEM/F12 and pipette up and down manually a further 80 times using moderate force. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Add 1 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 minutes. Remove the supernatant. The pellet should contain very little Matrigel at this stage. If Matrigel is still present, estimate its volume. Flick the tubes to re-suspend the pellets and place them on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
5. Working with one tube at a time, add ice-cold Matrigel, mix gently, and replace the tube on ice. Allow 20–25 µL of Matrigel per well to be plated, subtracting the estimated volume of any residual Matrigel remaining in the pellet. Pool organoids together and mix gently to distribute them evenly throughout the Matrigel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
6. Dispense 20–25 µL drops carefully onto the center of the growth area of wells in a 48-well culture plate, taking care not to create bubbles. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
7. Place the culture plate in the incubator for 15 minutes to allow the Matrigel to set. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
8. Add 250 µL of expansion medium to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
9. Replace the medium every 2–3 days. Passage the cultures every 7–10 days as appropriate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->

## Freezing

### Freezing

1. Remove the culture medium from the wells. Replace with 250 µL of Cell Recovery Solution (Corning) and place the plate on ice for 60 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Pool the contents of the wells into low-binding Eppendorf tubes using low-retention pipette tips. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 minutes to pellet the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Remove the supernatant and add 200 µL of Advanced DMEM/F12 to each tube. Manually pipette gently up and down 80 times with moderate force to partially disrupt the organoids. Add 1 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge again. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. Remove the supernatant and flick the pellets to re-suspend. Place the tubes on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
5. Add 0.5–1 mL of Recovery cell culture freezing medium (Life Technologies) to each tube with gentle mixing and transfer the contents to labeled cryovials on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
6. Transfer the cryovials immediately to a ‘Mr. Frosty' or similar cell freezing vessel at -80°C overnight, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->

## References

- [1] Derivation and long-term expansion of human endometrial and decidual organoids. — https://www.nature.com/protocolexchange/protocols/5779
